stem.text: A potentiometer circuit is used to determine the electromotive force (e.m.f.) $E_\text{X}$ of a cell. The circuit includes a second cell of known e.m.f. $E_0$ and negligible internal resistance, and a uniform resistance wire PQ of known length.
The movable connection J can be positioned anywhere along the length of the resistance wire.
Which circuit is suitable for determining $E_\text{X}$?

A.alt: Circuit diagram: wire PQ with a cell labelled E0 in a branch above it from P to Q; below, a cell labelled EX and a galvanometer in a branch from P to a sliding contact labelled J.

B.alt: Circuit diagram: wire PQ with a cell labelled EX in a branch above it from P to Q; below, a galvanometer and a cell labelled E0 in a branch from a sliding contact labelled J to Q.

C.alt: Circuit diagram: wire PQ with a branch above it from P to Q containing a galvanometer and a cell labelled E0; below, a cell labelled EX in a branch from P to a sliding contact labelled J.

D.alt: Circuit diagram: a cell labelled EX and a galvanometer in a branch from P to a sliding contact labelled J above wire PQ; below the wire, a cell labelled E0 in a branch from P to Q.
